He complained that Link wouldn't do everything that he wanted Link to do when he aimed the Wii Remote Plus at the TV screen, despite the fact that you do not, in fact, have to actually do that. McShea threw gasoline on the fire by giving an interview to justify his beliefs that people used to say "See - he really doesn't understand the controls!" If we're talking Twilight Princess, it's due to the fact that 8.8 wasn't the fabled 9.0 that any major game needed to have AAA status during the Gamespot System Wars "era". This was also compounded by the fact that Jeff Gerstmann, the reviewer, felt the Wii version was better than the Gamecube version, yet the Gamecube version scored an 8.9.

Jeff has never been a stranger to controversial review scores, and his scores have often been criticized for being way higher than the median (Tony Hawk Pro Skater games) or way lower than the median (like the flak he's catching for Fallout 4 today). Of course, Gamespot would eventually fire Gerstmann for his low reviews of Kane and Lynch 2 and other games, while also overhauling their reviews process multiple times, ditching reviews on each aspect of a game and assigning a score based on how each aspect is weighted, ditching the unfair and ambiguous "Tilt" score that graded games on a curve based on expectations, ditching the decimals for a .5 score, then ditching decimals altogether.
